summary: f-strings build text from values, with control over decimal places, column width, and alignment. Use them for reports, receipts, and tables.
notes: {average:.2f} shows 2 decimal places. It does not change the value stored in average.
{courses[i]:<12} pads the text to 12 characters, lined up on the left.
{7 / 8:.1%} multiplies by 100 for you, so 0.875 prints as 87.5%.
pitfall: Forgetting the f before the quotes prints the braces literally: "{student}" shows {student} instead of Jordan.
